movie.title: Yellow Letters
movie.overview: The marriage of Derya and Aziz is under pressure after losing their jobs because of state arbitrariness and moving to Istanbul to live with Aziz's parents. They and their 13-year-old daughter Ezgi have to redefine their way of life.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: After losing their livelihoods to authoritarian government persecution, a celebrated Turkish artist couple and their daughter relocate to Istanbul, where the strain of financial survival tests their marriage and moral principles.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: In Ankara, stage actress Derya and university professor Aziz lead a comfortable life with their 13-year-old daughter, Ezgi, until a subtle act of political defiance triggers swift retribution from the state. Both abruptly receive formal termination notices—the titular yellow letters—stripping them of their jobs, home, and standing. Forced to move into a cramped Istanbul apartment with Aziz's mother, the couple struggles to navigate systemic harassment and severe financial hardship. As Aziz stubbornly clings to his political principles while Derya makes quiet compromises to protect their future, growing ideological rifts threaten to fracture their family beyond repair.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Derya, an acclaimed theater actress, and Aziz, a university professor and playwright, enjoy a privileged existence in Ankara alongside their 13-year-old daughter, Ezgi. However, their comfortable reality disintegrates when Derya refuses a photo opportunity with a government official following a performance, and Aziz publicly encourages his students to engage in anti-establishment dialogue. The state responds with swift severity, issuing dismissal notices—known as 'yellow letters'—that strip the couple of their careers and subject Aziz to potential criminal charges. Facing pressure from landlords and law enforcement, the family is forced to abandon their Ankara home and relocate to Istanbul to live with Aziz's mother. Living in tight quarters while facing institutional censorship, the couple finds their dynamic deeply altered. Aziz holds onto his political integrity by working odd jobs and quietly continuing his subversive creative efforts, while Derya faces moral dilemmas as she seeks financial stability through state-sanctioned entertainment work. As financial hardship and political surveillance mount, 13-year-old Ezgi grows increasingly distant and rebellious amid her parents' constant conflict. Ultimately, Derya and Aziz must decide whether preserving their personal values is worth destroying the foundation of their family.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Directed by İlker Çatak, 'Yellow Letters' is an intimate political drama exploring the quiet, devastating impact of state censorship on private life. Set in modern-day Turkey, the narrative focuses on Derya and Aziz, a creative couple who seem to have achieved professional success and personal stability. Derya is a prominent stage actress, Aziz is an respected academic and playwright, and together they raise their 13-year-old daughter, Ezgi. Their life changes overnight when minor acts of political resistance draw the ire of government authorities. Delivered 'yellow letters'—official state notices terminating their employment—the couple is abruptly blacklisted from their respective fields, forcing them to move to Istanbul to stay with Aziz's mother. As the pressure of systemic persecution settles over their household, Derya and Aziz are forced to balance their artistic integrity with the practical realities of survival, driving a wedge between their shared values and their daughter's wellbeing.

story_structure.climax: Mounting economic hardship, legal risks, and ideological friction force Derya and Aziz to make a critical decision that directly pits their core convictions against their family's security.
story_structure.conflict: Following an incident at the premiere of their politically charged play, both parents receive arbitrary state dismissal notices ('yellow letters'), stripping them of their careers, income, and home.
story_structure.resolution: The family adapts to a complex new dynamic, navigating an ambiguous middle ground between artistic compromise and survival under systemic pressure.
story_structure.introduction: Derya and Aziz, a celebrated actor and drama professor living in Ankara with their 13-year-old daughter Ezgi, lead a fulfilling life centered around their artistic and intellectual work.
story_structure.risingAction: Forced to move to Istanbul to live with Aziz's mother, the family faces immense financial pressure; Aziz drives cabs while fighting legal battles, while Derya considers pragmatic artistic compromises, creating growing emotional distance between the parents and their daughter.
